verdict.rationale: LibreChat ships a Code Interpreter API (docs-10, docs-30) but this explicitly runs code 'securely' in a sandboxed environment, not on the user's own machine, and MCP support (docs-7, docs-24) can in principle be pointed at a filesystem MCP server to give real local file/command access — but that requires the user to stand up and expose their own machine as an MCP server themselves, it is not a built-in exec surface LibreChat provides out of the box. There is no evidence of LibreChat directly executing shell commands or editing files on the user's local filesystem as a first-party capability. Missing for 10: first-party local exec/file-edit tool (vs sandboxed interpreter), hands-on demonstration of MCP-based local file editing, and any confirmation this works without extra self-hosted MCP infrastructure.
